messages:
Ravi: FYI ACME hit a hard failure after the model swap to redwood-v3.2-quant in the canary cohort — invoice-generator tool now returns schema errors.
Priya: Customer says invoices failed in prod for ~20% of requests, they saw 400s and a billing spike. Need timeline + repro. :grimacing:
Ravi: Repro payload and error from their request (redacted):
```json
POST /v1/invoke
{
  \"tool\": \"invoice-generator\",
  \"input\": {\"order_id\": \"ORD-9912\", \"line_items\": \"item1,item2\", \"currency\": \"USD\"}
}

Response 400:
{\"error\":\"tool_schema_mismatch\", \"details\": \"line_items: expected array of objects, got string\"}
```
Ravi: They say same client works fine when routed to redwood-v3.1. Only fails hitting v3.2-quant canary.
Elena: @Ravi can you paste a runtime log for one of these failed invocations? Need to know if the model returned a bad shape or if our post-processor rejected it.
Ravi: Log snippet from runtime (sanitized):
```
2026-03-11T15:02:31Z req=xx123 model=redwood-v3.2-quant route=canary tool=invoice-generator status=400 schema_error=line_items:type_mismatch payload_from_model=\"[\u0022item1\u0022,\u0022item2\u0022]\"
```
Ravi: Looks like the model emitted a JSON-encoded string for the array instead of an actual array. v3.1 returned proper JSON array.
Noah: So the tool selection + schema validation is fine, the model's output shape changed. Did we change any decoder/serialization knobs in the v3.2 build?
Elena: We enabled an updated tokenizer/quantization path for v3.2-quant that alters whitespace/escape handling. Might be folding arrays into strings for certain templates. I want to reproduce locally.
Cory: Customer impact: invoice failures + extra retries caused unexpected token billing. We need a decision: pause canary or patch translation. Thoughts?
Priya: Customer already frustrated; recommending immediate rollback to v3.1 for that customer and pause global canary until root cause identified. Offer 1 day credit.
Elena: Agreed. Quick mitigation options: (1) server-side non-silent coercion: try to detect JSON-in-string and parse before schema check (fast patch), (2) rollback v3.2-quant canary to v3.1 (safest), (3) narrow routing: exclude invoice-generator tool from v3.2.
Ravi: Example of minimal server-side parse hack we tried in staging — it fixes this class of failure but could mask other regressions:
```python
# pseudo
if isinstance(model_output, str) and looks_like_json_array(model_output):
    model_output = json.loads(model_output)
validate_tool_schema(model_output)
```
Elena: That patch will stop immediate 400s but also hide model semantics changes. Product needs to decide if we want silent coercion.
Noah: Ops question: how fast can we rollback the canary? What's the current canary percent?
deploy-bot: canary roll to redwood-v3.2-quant at 2026-03-11T14:58Z, traffic=5%, cohorts=[default,acme-prod].
Noah: 5% and ACME is in cohort. We can toggle routing for ACME only or roll the entire canary back.
Cory: Prioritize ACME SLA — route ACME back to redwood-v3.1 and pause the global roll. We'll then decide whether to push a parsing shim or require model fix.
Ravi: Action items: 1) @Noah route ACME traffic -> redwood-v3.1 now. 2) @Elena reproduce locally + root cause. 3) @Priya notify ACME and offer credit + ETA. 4) @Cory coordinate decision on coercion vs model patch.
Noah: Routing change applied: ACME now on redwood-v3.1, verified by 200 responses for recently failing calls. Rolling pause on global canary initiated.
Priya: Messaging to ACME draft: "We've routed your traffic back to the previous model and are investigating. We can apply a credit for the impacted requests — apologies." :raised_hands:
Elena: Repro steps I used locally: start a local redwood runtime with v3.2-quant artifact, send the exact payload, compare model raw tokens. Confirmed model emitted a JSON string for arrays ~60% of runs for this prompt template. Collecting samples and opening a model-onboarding ticket.
Ravi: Customer confirms reduced errors after routing change. No more 400s in last 10 minutes.
Cory: We'll keep canary paused. If server-side coercion is considered, require a short-lived feature flag and strict logging so we can detect masked semantic regressions.
Noah: Filing incident follow-up for postmortem + SLO review. Assign @Elena to root cause and @Ravi to customer comms.
Ravi: Thanks all — will update thread after Elena's report. :thumbsup:
